strings.name: Martin van den Brink
strings.role: Former ASML President and CTO; Board advisor
strings.summary: Dutch engineer and technology leader Martin van den Brink joined ASML in 1984 and helped develop lithography systems, immersion and EUV technology. After retiring as President and CTO in 2024, he remained an advisor. His contributions depended on multidisciplinary teams and industry collaboration.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. ASML and ASM, current advisory work and former offices, and award announcement and conferment are distinguished. The honorary doctorate ceremony planned for November 27 has not yet occurred.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced ASML lithography systems engineering and EUV research, contributing to key equipment for advanced chip manufacturing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Engineering education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied electrical engineering at HTS Arnhem, entered applied physics at Twente in 1980 and graduated in 1984; final project concerned district heating.
strings.facts.f2.label: Technology management
strings.facts.f2.value: Became ASML Vice President Technology in 1995, joined its management board in 1999 and became President and CTO in 2013.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Lithography systems development
strings.highlights.h1.text: Contributed to alignment, TWINSCAN dual-stage, immersion and EUV technologies; entire systems are not individual inventions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Multidisciplinary engineering
strings.highlights.h2.text: University interview emphasizes connecting system-level thinking and specialist detail across optics, mechatronics, software and physics.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Honorary doctorate plan announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: Twente announces conferment planned for November 27; at the cutoff this is an announcement, not a completed award ceremony.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Receives alumni lifetime achievement award
strings.timeline.t2.text: University recap confirms an inaugural Van den Kroonenberg Oeuvre Award, alongside three other alumni.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Resigns ASM supervisory role
strings.timeline.t3.text: ASM announces immediate resignation to avoid possible future overlapping interests; not a finding of proven misconduct.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Retires as ASML President and CTO
strings.timeline.t4.text: Leaves executive management, remains Board advisor and is named an ASML Honorary Fellow in 2024.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Receives IEEE Noyce Medal
strings.timeline.t5.text: IEEE awards the Robert N. Noyce Medal for technical and managerial contributions to lithography.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes ASML President and CTO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Assumes technology leadership after years of engineering and technical management.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins ASML management board
strings.timeline.t7.text: Extends technical management into corporate governance; distinct from the later ASM supervisory role.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins early ASML
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joins as engineer in the company’s founding year; early employee does not mean legal founder.
